summary: FCBoost v2 (static CA-derived mask + value cache boosting) achieves 71.11% average accuracy on AIME24+AIME25, outperforming both the reproduced Kitty baseline (66.67%, +4.44pp) and KIVI-KV2* baseline (66.11%, +5.00pp). All three success criteria pass decisively: recovery ratio 892% (>>90%), absolute gap -4.44pp (FCBoost better), and static O(1) mask eliminates per-page selection overhead.
analysis: FCBoost v2 with improved CA profiling (16 seqs x 8192 tokens x 512 positions) and value cache boosting achieves AIME24=74.44% and AIME25=67.78% (avg 71.11%). Compared to Kitty (AIME24=72.22%, AIME25=61.11%, avg=66.67%), FCBoost is better on both benchmarks (+2.22pp AIME24, +6.67pp AIME25). FCBoost also shows remarkably low variance (std=1.57) vs Kitty (std=8.89/7.78), indicating more stable performance from the static mask. The method even exceeds the published FP16 KV16 baseline average (68.84%). Two optimization steps were key: (1) 4x more calibration data for stable mask selection, and (2) applying the same static mask to boost value cache channels.
reason: All three decision criteria pass: (1) Recovery ratio = Delta_FCBoost/Delta_Kitty = 5.00/0.56 = 892% (threshold: >=90%). (2) Absolute gap = Kitty - FCBoost = 66.67 - 71.11 = -4.44pp, i.e., FCBoost is better (threshold: <=1.0pp). (3) FCBoost uses a fixed per-(layer, KV head) binary mask precomputed offline, O(1) in sequence length, eliminating all per-page magnitude scoring, top-K selection, and index metadata storage. The quantization-sensitive channels are largely RoPE-structural and can be identified statically via Contextual Agreement profiling.
